candidates.title: Filter candidate programs against example tests from the problem statement
candidates.rule: For competitive-programming-style tasks whose statements include input/output examples, sample many solutions, discard those failing the public examples, and return the first survivor rather than an unfiltered sample.
candidates.passage: evaluating the first sample which passes the 3 public unit tests for each problem yields higher performance than raw pass@100 samples.
candidates.location: Section 3.5 Results on the APPS Dataset (Table 2)
candidates.finding: On APPS introductory problems, 1-shot Codex filtered pass@1 was 22.78% vs raw pass@100 of 20.20% and raw pass@1 of 4.14%; gains were much smaller for interview/competition tiers.
candidates.conditions: 1000 samples per task at temperature 0.6; one input/output example appended to the docstring as a formatting hint; 3-second execution timeout; sandboxed execution; some passing solutions were too slow.
candidates.limitations: Costly (1000 samples/task); public examples can be weak filters; absolute accuracy stayed very low on harder tiers; results are from a 2021 model and depend on having runnable example tests.
candidates.validation_test: On APPS or a similar benchmark with public examples, compare filtered pass@1 against raw pass@k at matched sample budgets, recording compute cost and timeout-failure rate.

reason: The paper reports concrete, tested sampling and selection interventions for code-generation models (temperature-by-k tuning, log-prob ranking vs random, filtering candidates against public example tests), plus a tested negative result on prompts containing bugs. These support scoped harness rules; BLEU/back-translation results support avoidance rules.
